verses: Handsome the suitor was and stout, Who for me in the lane looked out: I should have gone with him I doubt.
Can I that suitor's form forget, Who for me in the hall did wait? That I held off I now regret.

I'm here, my broidered upper robe Concealed beneath a garment plain. As lovely is my lower robe, With the same guard 'gainst travel stain. O sir, O sir, come and me hence convey; Your waiting chariot I shall not delay!

I'm here, my broidered lower robe Concealed beneath a garment plain. As lovely is my upper robe, With the same guard 'gainst travel stain. O sir, O sir, if you would only come, At once your chariot should convey me home!
